`struct A` contains exactly one complex member and its constructor `A(double r) : value{r, 0} {}` initializes the real part from `r` and the imaginary part to zero. There is no undefined behavior in the source: the complex object is fully initialized before use.

`test(const complex_t &c, const int &x)` takes the complex object by const reference and an integer by const reference. Its control flow is simple: if `x < 0` it prints `x`, otherwise it prints `__real__ c`, meaning only the real component of the complex argument is observed.

In the call site `test(a.value, 123)`, the branch condition is compile-time obvious: `123 < 0` is false. Under optimization, GCC is free to constant-fold the branch away and reduce the observable behavior to printing the real part of `a.value`.

`#pragma omp parallel num_threads(1)` causes OpenMP lowering even though only one thread is requested. This is important because the compiler still outlines the region into a worker function and applies OpenMP data-sharing/privatization rules, rather than executing the block as an ordinary lexical scope.

The local variable `A a{0.123};` lives inside the OpenMP parallel region, so it is private to the outlined worker function. The compiler must materialize and initialize this private object inside the outlined region before passing `a.value` to `test`.

The bug is not about concurrency or a race: with `num_threads(1)` there is only one executing thread. The failure shows a code-generation or optimization mistake in the outlined OpenMP path, not a synchronization issue.

The reported symptom is that the printed value becomes `0` instead of `0.123` only with `-O3` and `-fopenmp`. That means the frontend semantics are correct, but some optimization pass in the OpenMP-transformed program corrupts, drops, or mis-propagates the real component of the complex object.

Because the wrong output appears only at higher optimization and not in older GCC 12.4, the reproducer exercises a regression introduced in GCC 13-series development and persisting through GCC 14/15. The source is valid and stable across versions; the changed behavior is compiler-induced.

The bug report title mentions a regression since `r13-5681-ge8109bd87766be`, which strongly suggests the failure is tied to a specific optimization change affecting complex-type handling after OpenMP outlining or scalar replacement.

The issue reproduces with both built-in `__complex__` and `std::complex`, so the problem is unlikely to be limited to C++ library templates. It instead points to GCC's internal lowering/representation of complex values or aggregate stores/loads involving two-part floating data.

Sort all accesses for the given variable, check for partial overlaps and return NULL if there are any. Return the pointer to the first representative and make sure it is the first one in the vector of accesses.

gcc/tree-sra.cc.signature: static tree create_access_replacement (struct access *access, tree reg_type = NULL_TREE)
gcc/tree-sra.cc.summary: Create a variable for the given ACCESS which determines the type, name and a few other properties. Return the variable declaration and store it also to ACCESS->replacement. REG_TREE is used when creating a declaration to base a default-definition SSA name on in order to facilitate an uninitialized warning. It is used instead of the actual ACCESS type if that is not of a gimple register type.
Return ACCESS scalar replacement, which must exist.

Build a subtree of accesses rooted in *ACCESS, and move the pointer in the linked list along the way. Stop when *ACCESS is NULL or the access pointed to it is not "within" the root. Return false iff some accesses partially overlap.
Build a tree of access representatives, ACCESS is the pointer to the first one, others are linked in a list by the next_grp field. Return false iff some accesses partially overlap.
Traverse the access forest where ROOT is the first root and verify that various important invariants hold true.
Verify access forests of all candidates with accesses by calling verify_access_forest on each on them.
Return true if expr contains some ARRAY_REFs into a variable bounded array.

gcc/tree-sra.cc.signature: static bool analyze_access_subtree (struct access *root, struct access *parent, bool allow_replacements, bool totally)
gcc/tree-sra.cc.summary: Analyze the subtree of accesses rooted in ROOT, scheduling replacements when both seeming beneficial and when ALLOW_REPLACEMENTS allows it. If TOTALLY is set, we are totally scalarizing the aggregate. Also set all sorts of access flags appropriately along the way, notably always set grp_read and grp_assign_read according to MARK_READ and grp_write when MARK_WRITE is true. Creating a replacement for a scalar access is considered beneficial if its grp_hint ot TOTALLY is set (this means either that there is more than one direct read access or that we are attempting total scalarization) or according to the following table: Access written to through a scalar type (once or more times) | | Written to in an assignment statement | | | | Access read as scalar _once_ | | | | | | Read in an assignment statement | | | | | | | | Scalarize Comment ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- 0 0 0 0 No access for the scalar 0 0 0 1 No access for the scalar 0 0 1 0 No Single read - won't help 0 0 1 1 No The same case 0 1 0 0 No access for the scalar 0 1 0 1 No access for the scalar 0 1 1 0 Yes s = *g; return s.i; 0 1 1 1 Yes The same case as above 1 0 0 0 No Won't

gcc/tree-sra.cc.signature: static struct access * create_artificial_child_access (struct access *parent, struct access *model, HOST_WIDE_INT new_offset, bool set_grp_read, bool set_grp_write)
gcc/tree-sra.cc.summary: Create a new child access of PARENT, with all properties just like MODEL except for its offset and with its grp_write false and grp_read true. Return the new access or NULL if it cannot be created. Note that this access is created long after all splicing and sorting, it's not located in any access vector and is automatically a representative of its group. Set the gpr_write flag of the new accesss if SET_GRP_WRITE is true.

Beginning with ACCESS, traverse its whole access subtree and mark all sub-trees as written to. If any of them has not been marked so previously and has assignment links leading from it, re-enqueue it.
If there is still budget to create a propagation access for DECL, return true and decrement the budget. Otherwise return false.
Return true if ACC or any of its subaccesses has grp_child set.

Propagate all subaccesses across assignment links.
Return true if the forest beginning with ROOT does not contain unscalarizable regions or non-byte aligned accesses.

gcc/tree-sra.cc.summary: Create and return an ACCESS in PARENT spanning from POS with SIZE, TYPE and reference EXPR for total scalarization purposes and mark it as such. Within the children of PARENT, link it in between PTR and NEXT_SIBLING.

gcc/tree-sra.cc.summary: Create and return an ACCESS in PARENT spanning from POS with SIZE, TYPE and reference EXPR for total scalarization purposes and mark it as such, link it at *PTR and reshape the tree so that those elements at *PTR and their siblings which fall within the part described by POS and SIZE are moved to be children of the new access. If a partial overlap is detected, return NULL.

gcc/tree-sra.cc.signature: static bool access_and_field_type_match_p (tree outer, tree inner)
gcc/tree-sra.cc.summary: Return true if INNER is either the same type as OUTER or if it is the type of a record field in OUTER at offset zero, possibly in nested sub-records.

gcc/tree-sra.cc.signature: static enum total_sra_field_state total_should_skip_creating_access (struct access *parent, struct access **last_seen_sibling, tree type, HOST_WIDE_INT pos, HOST_WIDE_INT size)
gcc/tree-sra.cc.summary: Do all the necessary steps in total scalarization when the given aggregate type has a TYPE at POS with the given SIZE should be put into PARENT and when we have processed all its siblings with smaller offsets up until and including LAST_SEEN_SIBLING (which can be NULL). Return TOTAL_FLD_CREATE id the caller should carry on with creating a new access, TOTAL_FLD_DONE if access or accesses capable of representing the described part of the aggregate for the purposes of total scalarization already exist or TOTAL_FLD_FAILED if there is a problem which prevents total scalarization from happening at all.

Go over sub-tree rooted in ROOT and attempt to create scalar accesses spanning all uncovered areas covered by ROOT, return false if the attempt failed. All created accesses will have grp_unscalarizable_region set (and should be ignored if the function returns false).
Get the total total scalarization size limit in the current function.

Go through all accesses collected throughout the (intraprocedural) analysis stage, exclude overlapping ones, identify representatives and build trees out of them, making decisions about scalarization on the way. Return true iff there are any to-be-scalarized variables after this stage.

gcc/tree-sra.cc.signature: static void generate_subtree_copies (struct access *access, tree agg, HOST_WIDE_INT top_offset, HOST_WIDE_INT start_offset, HOST_WIDE_INT chunk_size, gimple_stmt_iterator *gsi, bool write, bool insert_after, location_t loc)
gcc/tree-sra.cc.summary: Generate statements copying scalar replacements of accesses within a subtree into or out of AGG. ACCESS, all its children, siblings and their children are to be processed. AGG is an aggregate type expression (can be a declaration but does not have to be, it can for example also be a mem_ref or a series of handled components). TOP_OFFSET is the offset of the processed subtree which has to be subtracted from offsets of individual accesses to get corresponding offsets for AGG. If CHUNK_SIZE is non-null, copy only replacements in the interval <start_offset, start_offset + chunk_size>, otherwise copy all. GSI is a statement iterator used to place the new statements. WRITE should be true when the statements should write from AGG to the replacement and false if vice versa. if INSERT_AFTER is true, new statements will be added after the current statement in GSI, they will be added before the statement otherwise.
Search for an access representative for the given expression EXPR and return it or NULL if it cannot be found.

gcc/tree-sra.cc.signature: static bool sra_modify_expr (tree *expr, gimple_stmt_iterator *gsi, bool write)
gcc/tree-sra.cc.summary: Replace the expression EXPR with a scalar replacement if there is one and generate other statements to do type conversion or subtree copying if necessary. GSI is used to place newly created statements, WRITE is true if the expression is being written to (it is on a LHS of a statement or output in an assembly statement).
Store all replacements in the access tree rooted in TOP_RACC either to their base aggregate if there are unscalarized data or directly to LHS of the statement that is pointed to by GSI otherwise.

gcc/tree-sra.cc.signature: static void load_assign_lhs_subreplacements (struct access *lacc, struct subreplacement_assignment_data *sad)
gcc/tree-sra.cc.summary: Try to generate statements to load all sub-replacements in an access subtree formed by children of LACC from scalar replacements in the SAD->top_racc subtree. If that is not possible, refresh the SAD->top_racc base aggregate and load the accesses from it.
Modify assignments with a CONSTRUCTOR on their RHS. STMT contains a pointer to the assignment and GSI is the statement iterator pointing at it. Returns the same values as sra_modify_assign.

gcc/tree-sra.cc.signature: static tree get_repl_default_def_ssa_name (struct access *racc, tree reg_type)
gcc/tree-sra.cc.summary: Create and return a new suitable default definition SSA_NAME for RACC which is an access describing an uninitialized part of an aggregate that is being loaded. REG_TREE is used instead of the actual RACC type if that is not of a gimple register type.

gcc/tree-sra.cc.signature: static void generate_subtree_deferred_init (struct access *access, tree init_type, tree decl_name, gimple_stmt_iterator *gsi, location_t loc)
gcc/tree-sra.cc.summary: Generate statements to call .DEFERRED_INIT to initialize scalar replacements of accesses within a subtree ACCESS; all its children, siblings and their children are to be processed. GSI is a statement iterator used to place the new statements.

For a call to .DEFERRED_INIT: var = .DEFERRED_INIT (size_of_var, init_type, name_of_var); examine the LHS variable VAR and replace it with a scalar replacement if there is one, also replace the RHS call to a call to .DEFERRED_INIT of the corresponding scalar relacement variable. Examine the subtree and do the scalar replacements in the subtree too. STMT is the call, GSI is the statment iterator to place newly created statement.

Examine both sides of the assignment statement pointed to by STMT, replace them with a scalare replacement if there is one and generate copying of replacements if scalarized aggregates have been used in the assignment. GSI is used to hold generated statements for type conversions and subtree copying.

Set any scalar replacements of values in the constant pool to the initial value of the constant. (Constant-pool decls like *.LC0 have effectively been initialized before the program starts, we must do the same for their replacements.) Thus, we output statements like 'SR.1 = *.LC0[0];' into the function's entry block.
Traverse the function body and all modifications as decided in analyze_all_variable_accesses. Return true iff the CFG has been changed.
Generate statements initializing scalar replacements of parts of function parameters.
The "main" function of intraprocedural SRA passes. Runs the analysis and if it reveals there are components of some aggregates to be scalarized, it runs the required transformations.
Perform early intraprocedural SRA.
Perform "late" intraprocedural SRA.
If type T cannot be totally scalarized, return false. Otherwise return true and push to the vector within PC offsets and lengths of all padding in the type as total scalarization would encounter it.
Given two types in an assignment, return true either if any one cannot be totally scalarized or if they have padding (i.e. not copied bits)

gcc/cp/semantics.cc.summary: Save the current deferred access states and start deferred access checking iff DEFER_P is true.
Save the current deferred access states and start deferred access checking, continuing the set of deferred checks in CHECKS.
Resume deferring access checks again after we stopped doing this previously.
Stop deferring access checks.
Discard the current deferred access checks and restore the previous states.
Returns a TREE_LIST representing the deferred checks. The TREE_PURPOSE of each node is the type through which the access occurred; the TREE_VALUE is the declaration named.
Take current deferred checks and combine with the previous states if we also defer checks previously. Otherwise perform checks now.

gcc/cp/semantics.cc.signature: static tree get_class_access_diagnostic_decl (tree parent_binfo, tree decl)
gcc/cp/semantics.cc.summary: Called from enforce_access. A class has attempted (but failed) to access DECL. It is already established that a baseclass of that class, PARENT_BINFO, has private access to DECL. Examine certain special cases to find a decl that accurately describes the source of the problem. If none of the special cases apply, simply return DECL as the source of the problem.

gcc/cp/semantics.cc.signature: static bool enforce_access (tree basetype_path, tree decl, tree diag_decl, tsubst_flags_t complain, access_failure_info *afi = NULL)
gcc/cp/semantics.cc.summary: If the current scope isn't allowed to access DECL along BASETYPE_PATH, give an error, or if we're parsing a function or class template, defer the access check to be performed at instantiation time. The most derived class in BASETYPE_PATH is the one used to qualify DECL. DIAG_DECL is the declaration to use in the error diagnostic.

Perform the access checks in CHECKS. The TREE_PURPOSE of each node is the BINFO indicating the qualifying scope used to access the DECL node stored in the TREE_VALUE of the node. If CHECKS is empty or we aren't in SFINAE context or all the checks succeed return TRUE, otherwise FALSE.

Perform the deferred access checks. After performing the checks, we still have to keep the list `deferred_access_stack->deferred_access_checks' since we may want to check access for them again later in a different context. For example: class A { typedef int X; static X a; }; A::X A::a, x; // No error for `A::a', error for `x' We have to perform deferred access of `A::X', first with `A::a', next with `x'. Return value like perform_access_checks above.

gcc/cp/semantics.cc.signature: bool perform_or_defer_access_check (tree binfo, tree decl, tree diag_decl, tsubst_flags_t complain, access_failure_info *afi)
gcc/cp/semantics.cc.summary: Defer checking the accessibility of DECL, when looked up in BINFO. DIAG_DECL is the declaration to use to print diagnostics. Return value like perform_access_checks above. If non-NULL, report failures to AFI.
Returns nonzero if the current statement is a full expression, i.e. temporaries created during that statement should be destroyed at the end of the statement.
T is a statement. Add it to the statement-tree. This is the C++ version. The C/ObjC frontends have a slightly different version of this function.
Returns the stmt_tree to which statements are currently being added.
If statements are full expressions, wrap STMT in a CLEANUP_POINT_EXPR.

Like maybe_cleanup_point_expr except have the type of the new expression be void so we don't need to create a temporary variable to hold the inner expression. The reason why we do this is because the original type might be an aggregate and we cannot create a temporary variable for that type.
Create a declaration statement for the declaration given by the DECL.

gcc/cp/semantics.cc.signature: static void set_cleanup_locs (tree stmts, location_t loc)
gcc/cp/semantics.cc.summary: Set EXPR_LOCATION of the cleanups of any CLEANUP_STMT in STMTS to LOC.
True iff the innermost block scope is a try block.

gcc/cp/semantics.cc.signature: void push_cleanup (tree decl, tree cleanup, bool eh_only)
gcc/cp/semantics.cc.summary: Queue a cleanup. CLEANUP is an expression/statement to be executed when the current scope is exited. EH_ONLY is true when this is not meant to apply to normal control flow transfer. DECL is the VAR_DECL being cleaned up, if any, or null for temporaries or subobjects.

Simple infinite loop tracking for -Wreturn-type. We keep a stack of all the current loops, represented by 'NULL_TREE' if we've seen a possible exit, and 'error_mark_node' if not. This is currently used only to suppress the warning about a function with no return statements, and therefore we don't bother noting returns as possible exits. We also don't bother with gotos.
A break is a possible exit for the current loop.
If we reach the end of the loop without seeing a possible exit, we have an infinite loop.

Finish such a conditional.

Finish a goto-statement.
Returns true if CALL is a (possibly wrapped) CALL_EXPR or AGGR_INIT_EXPR to operator= () that is written as an operator expression.

Finish an expression-statement, whose EXPRESSION is as indicated.

Returns true if FN, a CALL_EXPR, is a call to std::is_constant_evaluated or __builtin_is_constant_evaluated.

Process the COND of an if-statement, which may be given by IF_STMT.
Finish the then-clause of an if-statement, which may be given by IF_STMT.
Begin the else-clause of an if-statement.
Finish the else-clause of an if-statement, which may be given by IF_STMT.
Callback for cp_walk_tree to mark all {VAR,PARM}_DECLs in a tree as read.
Finish an if-statement.
Begin a while-statement. Returns a newly created WHILE_STMT if appropriate.

gcc/cp/semantics.cc.summary: Process the COND of a while-statement, which may be given by WHILE_STMT.
Finish a while-statement, which may be given by WHILE_STMT.
Begin a do-statement. Returns a newly created DO_STMT if appropriate.
Finish the body of a do-statement, which may be given by DO_STMT.

gcc/cp/semantics.cc.summary: Finish a do-statement, which may be given by DO_STMT, and whose COND is as indicated.
Finish a return-statement. The EXPRESSION returned, if any, is as indicated.
Begin the scope of a for-statement or a range-for-statement. Both the returned trees are to be used in a call to begin_for_stmt or begin_range_for_stmt.
Begin a for-statement. Returns a new FOR_STMT. SCOPE and INIT should be the return of begin_for_scope, or both NULL_TREE
Finish the init-statement of a for-statement, which may be given by FOR_STMT.

gcc/cp/semantics.cc.summary: Finish the COND of a for-statement, which may be given by FOR_STMT.
Finish the increment-EXPRESSION in a for-statement, which may be given by FOR_STMT.

gcc/cp/semantics.cc.summary: Finish the head of a range-based for statement, which may be given by RANGE_FOR_STMT. DECL must be the declaration and EXPR must be the loop expression.
Finish a break-statement.
Finish a continue-statement.
Begin a switch-statement. Returns a new SWITCH_STMT if appropriate.
Finish the cond of a switch-statement.
Finish the body of a switch-statement, which may be given by SWITCH_STMT. The COND to switch on is indicated.

Likewise, for a function-try-block. The block returned in COMPOUND_STMT is an artificial outer scope, containing the function-try-block.
Finish a try-block, which may be given by TRY_BLOCK.
Finish the body of a cleanup try-block, which may be given by TRY_BLOCK.
Finish an implicitly generated try-block, with a cleanup is given by CLEANUP.
Likewise, for a function-try-block.
Finish a handler-sequence for a try-block, which may be given by TRY_BLOCK.
Finish the handler-seq for a function-try-block, given by TRY_BLOCK. COMPOUND_STMT is the outer block created by begin_function_try_block.
Begin a handler. Returns a HANDLER if appropriate.
Finish the handler-parameters for a handler, which may be given by HANDLER. DECL is the declaration for the catch parameter, or NULL if this is a `catch (...)' clause.
Finish a handler, which may be given by HANDLER. The BLOCKs are the return value from the matching call to finish_handler_parms.

If BCS_FN_BODY is set, this is the outermost block of a function. If BCS_TRY_BLOCK is set, this is the block created on behalf of a TRY statement. Returns a token to be passed to finish_compound_stmt.
Finish a compound-statement, which is given by STMT.

gcc/cp/semantics.cc.summary: Finish an asm-statement, whose components are a STRING, some OUTPUT_OPERANDS, some INPUT_OPERANDS, some CLOBBERS and some LABELS. Also note whether the asm-statement should be considered volatile, and whether it is asm inline.

Finish a parenthesized expression EXPR.

Return TRUE iff EXPR_STMT is an empty list of expression statements.

Finish a use of `this'. Returns an expression for `this'.

gcc/cp/semantics.cc.summary: Finish a pseudo-destructor expression. If SCOPE is NULL, the expression was of the form `OBJECT.~DESTRUCTOR' where DESTRUCTOR is the TYPE for the type given. If SCOPE is non-NULL, the expression was of the form `OBJECT.SCOPE::~DESTRUCTOR'.

The set of allowed stack pointer modifications is small: (1) One or more auto-inc style memory references (aka pushes), (2) One or more addition/subtraction with the SP as destination, (3) A single move insn with the SP as destination, (4) A call_pop insn, (5) Noreturn call insns if !ACCUMULATE_OUTGOING_ARGS. Insns in the sequence that do not modify the SP are ignored, except for noreturn calls. The return value is the amount of adjustment that can be trivially verified, via immediate operand or auto-inc. gcc/expr.cc.signature: static void store_constructor_field (rtx target, poly_uint64 bitsize, poly_int64 bitpos, poly_uint64 bitregion_start, poly_uint64 bitregion_end, machine_mode mode, tree exp, int cleared, alias_set_type alias_set, bool reverse)
gcc/expr.cc.summary: Helper function for store_constructor. TARGET, BITSIZE, BITPOS, MODE, EXP are as for store_field. CLEARED is as for store_constructor. ALIAS_SET is the alias set to use for any stores. If REVERSE is true, the store is to be done in reverse order. This provides a recursive shortcut back to store_constructor when it isn't necessary to go through store_field. This is so that we can pass through the cleared field to let store_constructor know that we may not have to clear a substructure if the outer structure has already been cleared.

gcc/expr.cc.signature: static int fields_length (const_tree type)
gcc/expr.cc.summary: Returns the number of FIELD_DECLs in TYPE.

gcc/expr.cc.signature: void store_constructor (tree exp, rtx target, int cleared, poly_int64 size, bool reverse)
gcc/expr.cc.summary: Store the value of constructor EXP into the rtx TARGET. TARGET is either a REG or a MEM; we know it cannot conflict, since safe_from_p has been called. CLEARED is true if TARGET is known to have been zero'd. SIZE is the number of bytes of TARGET we are allowed to modify: this may not be the same as the size of EXP if we are assigning to a field which has been packed to exclude padding bits. If REVERSE is true, the store is to be done in reverse order.

gcc/expr.cc.signature: static rtx store_field (rtx target, poly_int64 bitsize, poly_int64 bitpos, poly_uint64 bitregion_start, poly_uint64 bitregion_end, machine_mode mode, tree exp, alias_set_type alias_set, bool nontemporal, bool reverse)
gcc/expr.cc.summary: Store the value of EXP (an expression tree) into a subfield of TARGET which has mode MODE and occupies BITSIZE bits, starting BITPOS bits from the start of TARGET. If MODE is VOIDmode, it means that we are storing into a bit-field. BITREGION_START is bitpos of the first bitfield in this region. BITREGION_END is the bitpos of the ending bitfield in this region. These two fields are 0, if the C++ memory model does not apply, or we are not interested in keeping track of bitfield regions. Always return const0_rtx unless we have something particular to return. ALIAS_SET is the alias set for the destination. This value will (in general) be different from that for TARGET, since TARGET is a reference to the containing structure. If NONTEMPORAL is true, try generating a nontemporal store. If REVERSE is true, the store is to be done in reverse order.

gcc/expr.cc.signature: tree get_inner_reference (tree exp, poly_int64_pod *pbitsize, poly_int64_pod *pbitpos, tree *poffset, machine_mode *pmode, int *punsignedp, int *preversep, int *pvolatilep)
gcc/expr.cc.summary: Given an expression EXP that may be a COMPONENT_REF, a BIT_FIELD_REF, an ARRAY_REF, or an ARRAY_RANGE_REF, look for nested operations of these codes and find the ultimate containing object, which we return. We set *PBITSIZE to the size in bits that we want, *PBITPOS to the bit position, *PUNSIGNEDP to the signedness and *PREVERSEP to the storage order of the field. If the position of the field is variable, we store a tree giving the variable offset (in units) in *POFFSET. This offset is in addition to the bit position. If the position is not variable, we store 0 in *POFFSET. If any of the extraction expressions is volatile, we store 1 in *PVOLATILEP. Otherwise we don't change that. If the field is a non-BLKmode bit-field, *PMODE is set to VOIDmode. Otherwise, it is a mode that can be used to access the field. If the field describes a variable-sized object, *PMODE is set to BLKmode and *PBITSIZE is set to -1. An access cannot be made in this case, but the address of the object can be found.

If C1 is odd to: (X - C2) * C3 <= C4 (or >), where C3 is modular multiplicative inverse of C1 and 1<<prec and C4 is ((1<<prec) - 1) / C1 or ((1<<prec) - 1) / C1 - 1 (the latter if C2 > ((1<<prec) - 1) % C1). If C1 is even, S = ctz (C1) and C2 is 0, use ((X * C3) r>> S) <= C4, where C3 is modular multiplicative inverse of C1>>S and 1<<prec and C4 is (((1<<prec) - 1) / (C1>>S)) >> S. We do not try to handle other cases as those would force us to fully cover the object with the CONSTRUCTOR node except for the components that are dead.
reviewed_methods.reason: Also highly plausible because the source constructs an aggregate/object inside the outlined OpenMP region, and GCC may represent part of that initialization as a CONSTRUCTOR store. If DSE incorrectly trims a constructor-based initialization, it could drop the bytes containing the real component or rewrite the store into an overly aggressive zeroing form. Slightly less direct than `maybe_trim_complex_store` because the bug report points more specifically to complex-lane mishandling than generic constructor trimming.

reviewed_methods.summary: Given a merged store group GROUP output the widened version of it. The store chain is against the base object BASE. Try store sizes of at most MAX_STORE_BITSIZE bits wide and don't output unaligned stores for STRICT_ALIGNMENT targets or if it's too expensive. Make sure that the number of statements output is less than the number of original statements. If a better sequence is possible emit it and return true.
reviewed_methods.reason: A credible optimization candidate because the object layout is effectively two adjacent doubles, and store merging could in principle widen or rewrite those stores incorrectly. The observed replacement of {0.123, 0.0} by an all-zero or wrong-lane result is compatible with a bad merged-store emission. Still, the regression's complex-specific nature makes tree-complex/SRA a bit more likely.

reviewed_methods.summary: Record the store STMT for store merging optimization if it can be optimized. Return true if any changes were made.
reviewed_methods.reason: Plausible but more indirect than output_merged_store. If store-merging misclassifies the complex-field initialization stores, later merging could go wrong. But this function mostly records candidates; the actual corruption would more likely happen during emitted transformed stores, or earlier during complex/SRA lowering.

reviewed_methods.summary: Lower the OpenMP parallel or task directive in the current statement in GSI_P. CTX holds context information for the directive.
reviewed_methods.reason: Reasonably plausible because it orchestrates outlining of the OpenMP parallel region and integrates later lowering steps. Since the bug only appears with -fopenmp, a mistake in task/parallel region lowering could expose the bad form later optimized incorrectly. Still, this feels more like an enabling context than the direct fix site.

A forward-propagation regression at O3 is believable, especially if OpenMP outlining and constant folding expose a bad SSA simplification. However, the observed failure is about losing the initialized real half of a complex object in memory/reference form, which is more naturally explained by store trimming than by this broad pass driver. This is plausible as the place where the bad transform is triggered, but less likely to be the precise fix point.

reviewed_methods.signature: void store_constructor (tree exp, rtx target, int cleared, poly_int64 size, bool reverse)
reviewed_methods.summary: Store the value of constructor EXP into the rtx TARGET. TARGET is either a REG or a MEM; we know it cannot conflict, since safe_from_p has been called. CLEARED is true if TARGET is known to have been zero'd. SIZE is the number of bytes of TARGET we are allowed to modify: this may not be the same as the size of EXP if we are assigning to a field which has been packed to exclude padding bits. If REVERSE is true, the store is to be done in reverse order.
reviewed_methods.reason: This is a reasonable lower-level suspect because it materializes constructor values and could mishandle partially zero complex/aggregate initialization. Still, the failure is optimization-sensitive (`-O3`) and regression-tied, which points more strongly to middle-end transformations such as DSE/SRA-like trimming than to stable generic expansion code. Worth considering, but not as strong as the DSE complex/constructor trimming routines.

reviewed_methods.reason: This is OpenMP-lowering code for receiver-side privatization and initialization, so it is relevant to outlined-region setup. However, the reproducer's object is a local variable declared inside the parallel region, not an input clause variable like firstprivate/copyin. That makes this less central than the complex- or SRA-specific candidates.

This should disappear, but is needed so we can combine expressions and use the fold() interfaces. Long term, we need to develop folding and combine routines that deal with gimple exclusively .
reviewed_methods.reason: This helper can affect how GIMPLE RHS expressions are reified for folding, so a complex-expression bug here is possible. But it is a generic conversion utility and does not by itself encode complex-lane trimming or OpenMP-private object semantics. It seems more like an indirect enabler than the most likely root fix location.

reviewed_methods.summary: For all elements of CLAUSES, validate them vs OpenMP constraints. Remove any elements from the list that are invalid.
reviewed_methods.reason: Unlikely as the best fix location. This is frontend clause validation/finalization logic, while the failure is optimization-sensitive, appears only at -O3, and affects both built-in and std::complex representations. The symptom strongly points to middle-end lowering/scalarization rather than clause semantic checking.
